messages:
jess: Heads-up — I just finished a holdout sweep for opti-embed-large-v2 (int8) on the dedicated eval cluster. Observed a recall@10 regression vs fp16 baseline on long-tail queries. Posting quick numbers and logs.

miguel: can you paste the exact eval command and dataset?

jess: sure — ran: 
```
python tools/eval_recall.py --model opti-embed-large-v2-int8 --dataset convo-holdout-2026 --k 10 --embed-batch 128 --index faiss_ivf4096_hnsw32
```
Baseline (fp16): recall@10 = 0.876
Int8 run: recall@10 = 0.842
Overall delta = -0.034 (-3.9%)
But segmented by cohort:
- short queries (<8 tokens): delta -0.004
- medium (8-32): delta -0.02
- long-tail (>32): delta -0.07 -> large drop on rare/technical queries

linh: that pattern screams quantization sensitivity in high-dim tail activations. Did you use per-channel quant or symmetric per-tensor?

jess: per-tensor symmetric (default from our quant pipeline). I also tried the 'calibrate-activations' option but used 1k calibration samples (random).

sam: two quick hypotheses:
1) per-channel int8 for weights may help; activations might need percentile clipping (e.g., 99.9) instead of max.
2) the FAISS index params could amplify small embedding shifts — check nprobe and distance metric (we use L2 with embeddings L2-normalized?).

jess: embeddings were NOT normalized before indexing in this run (my bad). Baseline runs used L2-normalized vectors. That could explain part of it. Re-running with normalization now.

miguel: ok that's important. Even small angular shifts change recall. Also try saving the raw fp16 embeddings from the same batch and computing cosine similarity directly (bypass index) to measure pure embedding drift.

linh: I'll queue two re-runs: (A) int8 per-channel + activation clipping(99.9) + normalized embeddings -> measure recall@10; (B) int8 per-tensor but with 10k calibration samples. Also produce mAP and recall@1/5/10.

jess: ty. Also capturing nearest-neighbor similarity delta distribution would help (cdf of cos similarity differences). Can we get histograms for the long-tail bucket?

eval-bot: Evaluation job 2026-03-18T14:22Z started: job_id=ev-4821. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/evals/ev-4821 :eyes:

sam: quick note — when you re-run, keep the same random seed and batching to avoid subtle cache / shard ordering differences. Also log embedding norms.

linh: queued. Expected runtimes ~45m each. I'll attach the script snippets in the thread once done.

jess: action items:
- linh: run A/B as above and post recall@1/5/10, mAP, histograms for long-tail (target by EOD)
- miguel: verify index config and run raw fp16 vs int8 cosine checks (I can hand over dataset)
- sam: draft a short note on recommended quant profiles for embeddings (per-channel + clipping) we can add to onboarding docs

miguel: quick command to compute raw recall (no index):
```
python tools/knn_naive.py --embed-file embeddings_{model}_{run}.npy --queries queries.npy --k 10 --metric cosine
```
Use --batch 256 to match throughput.

jess: thanks. if per-channel fixes it we can consider updating our quant pipeline defaults for embeddings. If not, we may need a lightweight retrain/finetune step or preserve fp16 for a small subset of vectors (hybrid).

linh: first run finished: int8 + per-channel + norm -> recall@10 = 0.868 (delta -0.008 vs fp16). Long-tail bucket now -0.012. attaching histogram link: https://internal.redwood/evals/ev-4821/hist

jess: good news. that's within acceptable range. can you also post raw cosine comparison numbers (int8 vs fp16) so we can quantify embedding distance shift?

linh: raw cosine mean delta = -0.0032, std = 0.021. Most of the mass near 0, tail at -0.12 correlates with poor recall examples.

sam: based on this, recommendation: default to per-channel quant + activation percentile clipping 99.9 and require L2-normalization before indexing. Add a CI check for long-tail recall delta > -0.02 — flag for manual review.

jess: agreed. I'll open a short PR to update the onboarding checklist and the quant pipeline defaults. Thanks everyone :party:
